report.source_text: Therapy according to the Euro-Lupus protocol was initiated, consisting of an intravenous steroid pulse (500 mg/day for 3 days), followed by oral methylprednisolone 0.8 mg/kg/day during the first month, afterwards slowly tapering the dose to 0.1 to 0.2 mg/kg/day. Cyclophosphamide (500 mg/day) was given six times, with an interval of 2 weeks. Along with this therapy, protective measures for gastrointestinal disease, candida infections, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, herpes infection, and osteoporosis was started. With this treatment regimen, disease control was obtained with complete clearance of the skin eruption and a normal urinalysis without proteinuria nor hematuria within 3 months after the start of treatment. DNA Farr titer became negative, and there was no more complement consumption. Steroids were tapered, and azathioprine as maintenance therapy was initiated at a dose of 1 mg/kg/day with maintained disease control during 4 months of follow-up.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Lupus nephritis class III-A (focal proliferative) according to the ISN/RPS 2003 classification
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old Caucasian woman presented with a 3-month history of photosensitive erythematous macules and papules on sun-exposed areas (thighs, back, arms, back of hands), with individual lesions lasting approximately 2 days and unresponsive to topical steroids. Skin biopsy revealed perivascular inflammatory infiltrate with leukocytoclasis, consistent with cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Urinalysis on admission showed proteinuria 2+ and massive hematuria with pyuria (WBC 32/µL), prompting investigation for systemic disease. Serologic workup demonstrated positive ANA with high dsDNA Farr titer, hypocomplementemia, and U1RNP positivity. Renal function assessment showed serum creatinine 0.82 mg/dL with GFR 77 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD-EPI, G2 category) and 24-hour proteinuria of 0.33 g; kidney ultrasound was normal. Kidney biopsy confirmed the diagnosis, demonstrating focal crescentic and focal mesangial glomerular damage with full-blown positivity of IgA, IgG, and C1q on immunohistochemistry, consistent with lupus nephritis class III-A (focal proliferative). Treatment with Euro-Lupus protocol (intravenous methylprednisolone pulse followed by oral corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide with azathioprine maintenance) resulted in complete clearance of skin eruption, normalization of urinalysis, negativity of DNA Farr titer, and restoration of complement levels within 3 months, with sustained disease control over 4 months of follow-up.

final.final_diagnosis: Lupus nephritis class III-A (focal proliferative) according to the ISN/RPS 2003 classification
final.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old Caucasian woman presented with a 3-month history of photosensitive erythematous macules and papules on sun-exposed areas (thighs, back, arms, back of hands), with individual lesions lasting approximately 2 days and unresponsive to topical steroids. Skin biopsy revealed perivascular inflammatory infiltrate with leukocytoclasis, consistent with cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Urinalysis on admission showed proteinuria 2+ and massive hematuria with pyuria (WBC 32/µL), prompting investigation for systemic disease. Serologic workup demonstrated positive ANA with high dsDNA Farr titer, hypocomplementemia, and U1RNP positivity. Renal function assessment showed serum creatinine 0.82 mg/dL with GFR 77 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD-EPI, G2 category) and 24-hour proteinuria of 0.33 g; kidney ultrasound was normal. Kidney biopsy confirmed the diagnosis, demonstrating focal crescentic and focal mesangial glomerular damage with full-blown positivity of IgA, IgG, and C1q on immunohistochemistry, consistent with lupus nephritis class III-A (focal proliferative). Treatment with Euro-Lupus protocol (intravenous methylprednisolone pulse followed by oral corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide with azathioprine maintenance) resulted in complete clearance of skin eruption, normalization of urinalysis, negativity of DNA Farr titer, and restoration of complement levels within 3 months, with sustained disease control over 4 months of follow-up.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Photosensitive cutaneous manifestation consistent with lupus erythematosus
Skin biopsy findings consistent with lupus erythematosus
Serologic evidence of systemic lupus erythematosus
Kidney biopsy confirming lupus nephritis class III-A (focal proliferative)

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Although initially suspected based on clinical presentation and skin biopsy findings, the positive ANA with high dsDNA Farr titer, proteinuria, massive hematuria, and kidney biopsy findings demonstrating focal crescentic and mesangial glomerular damage with IgA, IgG, and C1q positivity established the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus nephritis class III-A rather than isolated urticarial vasculitis

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Other forms of lupus nephritis (classes I, II, IV, V, VI)
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Kidney biopsy histopathology showing focal crescentic and focal mesangial glomerular damage with immunohistochemical findings of IgA, IgG, and C1q positivity specifically fits the ISN/RPS 2003 classification of class III-A (focal proliferative) lupus nephritis, not other classes

remaining_uncertainties: Direct immunofluorescence findings on skin biopsy (IgG, IgM, IgA, C3, C1q pattern at dermal-epidermal junction) were not reported in available records
Specific complement levels (C3 and C4 values) were not explicitly documented, though hypocomplementemia was noted
Complete blood count findings (hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelet count, WBC differential) were not retrieved from available records
